This repository's profile and review notes: the console entry point, the identity types, and the reviewed statement that no single account ID, alias or password form is inferred. They hold no markup.

KeePassXC-Browser's site list at commit 8b0b2c4: sign-in is treated as a multi-page flow on signin.aws.amazon.com (line 16, an entry from 2020), and the submit button has the id signin_button and sits outside the form (lines 231-236, from 2021). No input field is described, and both entries are about five years old.

Chromium's public password-manager site tests (commit 88f1fe85) hold no recipes: they are kept in an internal repository. Mozilla's published password recipes (13 records, read 2026-10-12) have no entry for an AWS host.
neededFromUser: In your own browser, signed out: open https://console.aws.amazon.com/ with the identity you use (root user or IAM user) and save the first sign-in page; enter the user name, continue, and save the password page before typing the password. Note the address of each up to the question mark. Save each as Webpage, Complete (HTML only re-downloads the address and misses a scripted or submitted form). Keep the files outside the repository: they can hold your account name. Import: node scripts/capture-login-page.mjs --id aws-console --from-file <file.html>
schemaGaps: An IAM user signs in with three values: the account ID or alias, the user name and the password (this repository's profile text). The steps format types a username and a password and has no third value. Root-user sign-in may fit the format; its fields are not established.
notes: The three AWS partitions are separate applications with separate hosts. What is recorded here concerns the commercial partition only.
